conviction_note: The findings sum to +3.2: an inferred revenue beat from Kiniksa's own sequential trajectory, a fourth guidance raise in a row, and small positioning and management items, less a small gross-to-net drag. The scaled number is (2*0.58-1)*12 = +1.92. p_up is held at 58 because the beat case is an inference from public company numbers that the buy-side can run too, and because this name sold beats in Oct 2025, Jan 2026 and Feb 2026 even though it bought them in Apr and Jul 2026. The gap between +3.2 and +1.92 is that uncertainty about the reaction, not a disagreement about the sign.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue (all ARCALYST net product revenue): consensus $260.66M, EPS $0.371 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-27-kiniksa-pharmaceuticals-ltd-stock/, read 2026-10-26). A second MarketBeat snippet gives $260.2M and $0.3722, so both estimates come from one vendor family. The company's own guide supports the bar: 2026 ARCALYST guidance of $980-995M (Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1730430/000173043026000031/knsa-20260728xex99d1.htm) less H1 actuals of $457.9M (Q1 $214.3M + Q2 $243.6M) implies H2 of $522-537M, or $261-268M a quarter. Consensus therefore sits at the low edge of the company's implied run rate. My estimate is about $268M (+3%).

The stock was down 6.4% intraday on 2026-10-26 to about $71.8 at 13:36 ET on roughly average volume (MarketBeat), and I found no company-specific news for it.

findings.finding: Kiniksa's own reported quarters imply a Q3 revenue beat. ARCALYST net revenue went Q1'25 $137.8M, Q2'25 $156.8M (+19.0), Q3'25 $180.9M (+24.1), Q4'25 $202.1M (+21.2), Q1'26 $214.3M (+12.2, the seasonal Q1 dip), Q2'26 $243.6M (+29.3). The $260.7M Q3 consensus implies only +$17.1M sequentially, below every non-Q1 increment since Q1 2025. Management also said at the 2026-09-09 Wells Fargo conference that Q2 new-patient enrollment was the highest of any quarter since launch and that gross-to-net is seasonally lowest in Q2-Q3. A repeat of the +$21-29M non-Q1 increments gives $265-273M, a 2-5% beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: revenue $243.6M vs $226.5M consensus (+7.5%) with a guide raise, stock +25.0%. Q1'26: $214.3M vs about $206M consensus (+4%) with a raise, +23.5%. But Q3'25 (2025-10-28) -2.9%, the Q4'25 pre-announcement (2026-01-12) -6.1% and the FY25 print with a first 2026 guide (2026-02-24) -8.2%. So 2026 beats have been bought hard, while late-2025 prints fell. Sources: baseline history; https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/kiniksa-pharmaceuticals-international-nasdaqknsa-given-new-10700-price-target-at-jpmorgan-chase-co-2026-07-29/
findings.why_not_priced: If the street had priced a Q3 above $265M, the published consensus would sit there rather than at $260.7M, which is the low edge of the guide's implied H2 run rate. The stock also would not have fallen 10% in five sessions, and 6% intraday today, into the print. The obvious counter: the buy-side whisper is probably above $260.7M. That is why this is sized below the name's 2026 reactions and why p_up stays at 58.
findings.independence: Same company dataset across the Q1/Q2 2026 and Q4 2025 8-K exhibits (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1730430/000173043026000014/knsa-20260224xex99d1.htm). The demand commentary comes from a different document, the 2026-09-09 Wells Fargo conference summary (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/kiniksa-at-wells-fargo-conference-arcalyst-growth-and-pipeline-deepen-93CH-4893796): record Q2 new-patient enrollment, penetration up from 18% to 21% of about 14,000 multiple-recurrence patients over two quarters, first-recurrence share up from about 15% to about 20%. Shares the trajectory basis with the guidance finding below.

findings.finding: Kiniksa has raised its 2026 ARCALYST guide at every 2026 print: initial $900-920M (2026-02-24), then $930-945M (2026-04-28), then $980-995M (2026-07-28). A Q3 near $268M plus a Q4 near the trend ($285-295M) puts the year at roughly $1,010-1,020M. That is above the top of the current range, so a fourth raise to about $1.0B or more is the likely shape of the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two 2026 raises (+$30M midpoint in April, +$50M in July) came with +23.5% and +25.0% reactions. The first 2026 guide in February (900-920) came with -8.2%. Raise size and direction have decided this name's reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of it is priced. A raise is the expected base case after two in a row, so only the size can surprise. If the market expected a raise of more than $20-30M the stock would not be 14% off its high into the print. Sized small because the base case is a raise and the street knows the pattern.
findings.independence: Rests on the same company revenue series as the trajectory finding. The independent part is the company's behaviour (three guides in 2026, each higher): Q1 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001730430/000173043026000017/knsa-20260428xex99d1.htm and FY25 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1730430/000173043026000014/knsa-20260224xex99d1.htm. Not a second fact.

findings.finding: Gross-to-net pressure. At the 2026-09-09 Wells Fargo conference management cited higher co-pay utilization and changes to co-pay support programs and described 'some pressure on gross-to-net', while still calling the pattern seasonal: highest in Q1, lower in Q2-Q3, modest rebound in Q4. This is a source of downside to net price per patient in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned visibly on gross-to-net. Revenue (volume) has been the line.
findings.why_not_priced: It was said publicly at a conference, so it is mostly priced. It sits here because it is the one company-sourced item pointing against the beat. The aggregator write-up contains date errors ('Q2 2024'), so the exact wording is uncertain.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the demand commentary in the first finding. One document, read in both directions, so the two are netted here rather than counted twice.

findings.finding: Into the print the stock fell 9.9% over 5 sessions and about 6.4% intraday on 2026-10-26 (to about $71.8, low $70.67) with no company news, while biotech (XBI) had been pulling back since September on failed readouts and rates. Short interest is 10.1% of float with 6.4 days to cover, and option open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.04). The bar on the tape is lower than at the 52-week high of $83-84 set after the July beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print came off a lower base and went +25%. No measured history of pre-print drawdowns on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is by definition in the price. The finding is that de-risking into the print lowers the bar a beat has to clear. An unexplained drawdown can also be informed selling, which is why this is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Sector pullback context from a different source: https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/biotech-charts-xbi-private-public-merger-acquisition-deals/832398/ (XBI off about 7% over the month into early October 2026). That is a proxy, not company-specific.

findings.finding: 8-K filed 2026-10-22: Ross Moat (EVP and COO since 2019, runs commercial, clinical, regulatory and manufacturing) was promoted to President and COO effective 2026-10-17, reporting to Chairman and CEO Sanj Patel. No departure was disclosed, and salary rises from $650k to $700k from 2027-01-01. A commercial-continuity signal five days before the print rather than a management exit.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and probably priced. A quiet 8-K that no preview mentions. A promotion before a print weakly signals no bad internal news. A clear signal would have been a departure.

outside_window.finding: Competitor: Cardiol Therapeutics said on 2026-09-23 that its pivotal Phase III MAVERIC trial of oral CardiolRx in recurrent pericarditis reached its enrollment target ahead of schedule and was expanded, with the primary endpoint now time to first recurrence. The readout is after this window. It is a long-term overhang on ARCALYST and may draw questions on the call.

Competitor: Lilly bought Ventyx (about $1.2B). Ventyx's NLRP3 inhibitor VTX2735 is in Phase 2 for recurrent pericarditis, with a Phase 3 start targeted for H2 2026 per pre-deal guidance. No readout falls inside the window.

lessons_applied: Lesson 3 (the caveat has to reach the number): the trajectory finding cited the Wells Fargo transcript only in its favour. The same transcript's gross-to-net and co-pay pressure is now filed as its own -0.3 finding, so judges see both readings of one document.

Lesson 6 (inside what was guided): the guidance-raise finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8, because a raise is the expected base case after two consecutive raises and consensus sits inside the guide's implied H2.
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth about 0; proxy transmission is small): the positioning finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Executive-promotion finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1. It is a weak signal with no reaction history.
Lesson 1 (the reaction function has a veto) was already reflected: p_up held at 58 because late-2025 prints were sold despite growth. abs_move_pct (12) and p_up are unchanged.
